correctness.rationale: For all m≥1, arbitrary Borel copulas with uniform marginals and all normalized real trigonometric polynomials are handled by a direct inequality. Sine/cosine test pairs bound worst risk by (1+max c_k)/2. The Fejer sum identity with strictly positive triangular weights forces max c_k≥−1/m. Uniform random nonidentity (m+1)th-root displacement yields all complex moments −1/m and therefore exactly isotropic risk (m−1)/(2m). Equality forces vanishing geometric sum almost surely and all cosine moments −1/m; a double-angle calculation rules out fixed shifts for m≥3. Standalone finite checks passed 2341 tests but are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The fixed-marginal, two-evaluation integration problem has a natural finite Fourier norm criterion. The new sharp universal copula optimum is achieved by a finite random shift that equalizes risk across all 2m directions, and every optimum has highly constrained root-of-unity difference support; a deterministic fixed shift fails from bandwidth m=3 onward. Improvement against iid is 1/m, meaningful especially at small bandwidth, with no claim of large-bandwidth universal speedup.
